content.text:
Neither `research.json` nor `tree.gedcomx.json` exist in the project directory, so there is no existing 1880 census source entry to refine. Per the instructions, nothing will be written to disk. Below is the properly structured Evidence Explained citation for the 1880 United States Federal Census, with bracketed placeholders for every element that must come from the actual record image.

---

**Formatted citation (footnote style)**

> 1880 U.S. Census, [County] County, [State], population schedule, [Township or City], enumeration district [ED number], supervisor's district [SD number], sheet [sheet number], [Head of Household] household, dwelling [dwelling number], family [family number]; NARA microfilm publication T9, roll [roll number]; digital image, [FamilySearch.org *or* Ancestry.com], accessed [Day Month Year].

**citation_detail (six-field structure)**

```json
{
  "who": "U.S. Census Bureau",
  "what": "1880 U.S. Census, [County] County, [State], population schedule",
  "when_created": "1880",
  "when_accessed": "[date accessed]",
  "where": "[FamilySearch.org or Ancestry.com] (NARA microfilm publication T9, roll [roll number])",
  "where_within": "[Township or City], enumeration district [ED number], supervisor's district [SD number], sheet [sheet number], [Head of Household] household, dwelling [dwelling number], family [family number]"
}
```

**Gaps — supply these from the record image**

- County, State, and township or city name
- Enumeration district number and supervisor's district number (both printed at the top of each schedule page)
- Sheet number (also at the top of the page; note whether it is the front [A] or back [B] side)
- Dwelling number and family number (from columns 1 and 2 of the schedule)
- Head of household name (for the `[Head of Household] household` locator; use the name recorded on the schedule, not the research subject's name if they are a child in the household)
- NARA microfilm T9 roll number (shown on the FamilySearch or Ancestry record detail page)
- Access date

**Nothing was written to disk.** No source entry exists to refine, so no changes were made to `research.json`.

---

The 1880 census citation above follows the Evidence Explained layered-path format: the digital access point first, then the NARA microfilm it reproduces, with all the physical locators (enumeration district, supervisor's district, sheet, dwelling, and family number) that let another person turn to the exact page. Every bracketed item needs to be read off the record image or its index page — the citation cannot be fully completed without those values in hand.

To save this citation once you have a source entry, bring the filled-in values back and the citation agent will refine the existing entry in place.
